@feoh ah, to be clear—specifically I don’t believe the merits of Gatsby are relevant if they are retiring the thing

Perhaps controversially—I believe the same could very easily happen to any VC-funded framework.

What happens when you have multiple FTE on payroll and you exhaust your runway without a viable strategy to monetize?

After working in the industry for 25+ years, I feel like VC-funded open source is a terrible idea. Whenever possible, we should be taking the hit and getting the projects under foundations (Apache, Open JSF). They add processes to the project which can slow things down but helps protect maintainers/users from the insanity.

Getting down off my soap-box.

@brianleroux @boneskull @zachleat This is my favorite takeaway. The reason to target JS was that it was "close to the metal" in terms of portable Web media; the entire cottage industry of "transpiler to JS" is built upon that requirement. I can't help but speculate that WASM is part of the picture; the overwhelming complexity had to collapse somehow, and shifting foundations would be a reasonable cause.

There was discussion about this recently, on Lobsters: https://lobste.rs/s/id9jet/transpiler_meaningless_word

@zachleat I can confidently report that working for a VC -funded startup is almost always going to end in tears for the employees.

It was a Friday. The 23 FTEs who were fired that morning went on to other work, often unrelated to their jobs at the startup (for the love of the gods, don’t work for a VC startup as a career ladder step. I don’t even know where to start on that idea), but the leaders of the company have vanished into obscurity.
@VickieGray whew, it’s sounding more common the longer I’m in the game

@corbin @boneskull @zachleat text to text is pretty lossy and interpreted code always on a back foot wrt optimization so wasm def seems inevitable.

@zachleat Perhaps I'm too cynical, but it seems to me that the focus shifts to enterprise whenever a technology is past the peak of its adoption curve. This maximizes profit during the long tail of usage by users that are more locked into the technology (usually big orgs that can't turn on a dime). In this case, it's not really about Gatsby, but about React more broadly, and where people perceive it to be in the tech cycle.

@lekoarts @zachleat OK, but as Ward says in there the goal wasn't really to implement RSC - it was to find a solution to support partial hydration. Do you think Gatsby needs full RSC support, or just fix the current implementation?

@ascorbic @zachleat Ok, sorry, my answer was a bit vague. I meant: Implement RSC (but not fully) in a way that makes most sense for Gatsby to e.g. achieve island architecture and possible other improvements (innovation needed here). So short term make Partial Hydration production-ready.
